chunks: And my father (may Allah have mercy on him mercy) narrated to me from Sa'd ibn 'Abdillah, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa, from Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from Al-Khaybari, from Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad Al-Qummi, from Abu Al-Hasan Al-Rida (peace be upon him), who said:
Whoever goes to the Ziyarah of the grave of Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) by the shore of the Euphrates is like the one who has gone to the Ziyarah of Allah above [in] His Throne.

key_terms.أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Abu 'Abdillah (title of Imam Al-Husayn ibn 'Ali, peace be upon him)
key_terms.بِشَطِّ الْفُرَاتِ: By the shore of the Euphrates (referring to Karbala)

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual significance of visiting Imam Husayn's grave by the Euphrates?
ai.summary: This hadith from Ibn Qulawayh’s *Kamil al-Ziyarat* elevates the physical act of visiting Imam Al-Husayn’s grave in Karbala to a metaphysical encounter with the Divine, reflecting the Shia doctrine of *Tajalli* (Divine manifestation) in the Ahlulbayt. By equating this ziyarah to 'visiting Allah on His Throne,' it underscores the Imam’s role as the ultimate locus of God’s presence and authority (*Hujjah*) on earth, a concept deeply rooted in Shia exegesis of verses describing God’s nearness and dominion.
